62044-billy-and-hans-my-squirrel-friends.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. with their delicate anatomy, so marvellously like the human hand in their flexibility and handiness, and the graceful curl of his tail, settled the question of genus; and mindful of my boyhood and a beloved pet of the American species of his genus, I bought him and named him Billy.

71600-true-heroism.title: True Heroism.
71600-true-heroism.creator: Unknown
71600-true-heroism.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. For want of something better to do, Willy, quietly seated in the corner, was cutting a round hole in his drum; a box of paints lay on the table, with which Bella had been daubing, certainly not adorning, the plates in the last book which her uncle had given her. There was a broken draughts-board under the table, but half of the draughtsmen were lost, and Tom and Louis, who had taken to chess, were beginning to quarrel over the game.

arxiv-2108-00507.title: Gate controlled quantum dots in monolayer WSe 2
arxiv-2108-00507.creator: Justin Boddison-Chouinard, Alex Bogan, Norman Fong, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Sergei Studenikin, Andrew Sachrajda, Marek Korkusinski, Abdulmenaf Altintas, Maciej Bieniek, Pawel Hawrylak, Adina Luican-Mayer ∗, Louis Gaudreau ∗
arxiv-2108-00507.description: Abstract Quantum confinement and manipulation of charge carriers are critical for achieving devices practical for quantum technologies. The interplay between electron spin and valley, as well as the possibility to address their quantum states electrically and optically, make two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides an emerging platform for the development of quantum devices.

arxiv-2109-01673.title: Brightest Cluster Galaxies Trace Weak Lensing Mass Bias and Halo Triaxiality in The Three Hundred Project 2021 Brightest Cluster Galaxies Trace Weak Lensing Mass Bias and Halo Triaxiality in The Three Hundred Project – References
arxiv-2109-01673.creator: Ricardo Herbonnet, Adrian Crawford, Camille Avestruz, Elena Rasia, Carlo Giocoli, Massimo Meneghetti, Anja von der Linden, Weiguang Cui, Gustavo Yepes
arxiv-2109-01673.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ricardo Herbonnet, Adrian Crawford, Camille Avestruz, Elena Rasia, Carlo Giocoli, Massimo Meneghetti, Anja von der Linden, Weiguang Cui, Gustavo Yepes. Galaxy clusters have a triaxial matter distribution. The weak-lensing signal, an important part in cosmological studies, measures the projected mass of all matter along the line-of-sight, and therefore changes with the orientation of the cluster.

arxiv-2110-03765.title: Spectroscopy Approaches for Food Safety Applications: Improving Data Efficiency Using Active Learning and Semi-Supervised Learning
arxiv-2110-03765.creator: Huanle Zhang, Nicharee Wisuthiphaet, Hemiao Cui, Nitin Nitin, Xin Liu, Qing Zhao
arxiv-2110-03765.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Huanle Zhang, Nicharee Wisuthiphaet, Hemiao Cui, Nitin Nitin, Xin Liu, Qing Zhao. The past decade witnessed rapid development in the measurement and monitoring technologies for food science. Among these technologies, spectroscopy has been widely used for the analysis of food quality, safety, and nutritional properties. Due to the complexity of food systems and the lack of comprehensive predictive models, rapid and simple measurements to predict complex properties in food systems are largely missing.

arxiv-2211-03837.title: AX-MABSA: A Framework for Extremely Weakly Supervised Multi-label Aspect Based Sentiment Analysis
arxiv-2211-03837.creator: Sabyasachi Kamila, Walid Magdy, Sourav Dutta, MingXue Wang
arxiv-2211-03837.description: Abstract Aspect Based Sentiment Analysis is a dominant research area with potential applications in social media analytics, business, finance, and health. Prior works in this area are primarily based on supervised methods, with a few techniques using weak supervision limited to predicting a single aspect category per review sentence.

arxiv-2302-06686.title: VERITAS and Fermi -LAT constraints on the Gamma-ray Emission from Superluminous Supernovae SN2015bn and SN2017egm Journal: ApJ https://veritas.sao.arizona.edu fermipy (v0.19), ( Wood et al. 2017 ) , astropy ( Robitaille et al. 2013 ; Price-Whelan et al. 2018 ) , CTOOLs, ( Knödlseder et al. 2016b ) ,
arxiv-2302-06686.creator: A. Acharyya, C. B. Adams, P. Bangale, W. Benbow, J. H. Buckley, M. Capasso, V. V. Dwarkadas, M. Errando, A. Falcone, Q. Feng, J. P. Finley, G. M. Foote, L. Fortson, A. Furniss, G. Gallagher, A. Gent, W. F Hanlon, O. Hervet, J. Holder, T. B. Humensky, W. Jin, P. Kaaret, M. Kertzman, M. Kherlakian, D.
arxiv-2302-06686.description: Abstract Superluminous supernovae (SLSNe) are a rare class of stellar explosions with luminosities ∼ {\sim} 10–100 times greater than ordinary core-collapse supernovae. One popular model to explain the enhanced optical output of hydrogen-poor (Type I) SLSNe invokes energy injection from a rapidly spinning magnetar.

arxiv-2307-03738.title: QIGen: Generating Efficient Kernels for Quantized Inference on Large Language Models
arxiv-2307-03738.creator: Tommaso Pegolotti, Elias Frantar, Dan Alistarh, Markus Püschel
arxiv-2307-03738.description: Abstract We present ongoing work on a new automatic code generation approach for supporting quantized generative inference on LLMs such as LLaMA or OPT on off-the-shelf CPUs. Our approach is informed by the target architecture and a performance model, including both hardware characteristics and method-specific accuracy constraints.

arxiv-2310-05109.title: Lightweight In-Context Tuning for Multimodal Unified Models
arxiv-2310-05109.creator: Yixin Chen, Shuai Zhang, Boran Han, Jiaya Jia
arxiv-2310-05109.description: Abstract In-context learning (ICL) involves reasoning from given contextual examples. As more modalities comes, this procedure is becoming more challenging as the interleaved input modalities convolutes the understanding process. This is exemplified by the observation that multimodal models often struggle to effectively extrapolate from contextual examples to perform ICL.

arxiv-2310-15481.title: Detecting anomalous images in astronomical datasets
arxiv-2310-15481.creator: Pedro Alonso, Jun Zhang, Xiao-Dong Li
arxiv-2310-15481.description: Abstract Environmental and instrumental conditions can cause anomalies in astronomical images, which can potentially bias all kinds of measurements if not excluded. Detection of the anomalous images is usually done by human eyes, which is slow and sometimes not accurate.

arxiv-2410-12069.title: De-jargonizing Science for Journalists with GPT-4: A Pilot Study Conference: Computation+Journalism Symposium; October 25–27, 2024; Boston, MA
arxiv-2410-12069.creator: Sachita Nishal, Eric Lee, Nicholas Diakopoulos
arxiv-2410-12069.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sachita Nishal, Eric Lee, Nicholas Diakopoulos. This study offers an initial evaluation of a human-in-the-loop system leveraging GPT-4 (a large language model or LLM), and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to identify and define jargon terms in scientific abstracts, based on readers’ self-reported knowledge. The system achieves fairly high recall in identifying jargon and preserves relative differences in readers’ jargon identification, suggesting personalization as a feasible use-case for LLMs to support sense-making of complex information.

arxiv-2505-10806.title: RapidGNN: Communication Efficient Large-Scale Distributed Training of Graph Neural Networks
arxiv-2505-10806.creator: Arefin Niam, M S Q Zulkar Nine
arxiv-2505-10806.description: Abstract Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have achieved state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance in diverse domains. However, training GNNs on large-scale graphs poses significant challenges due to high memory demands and significant communication overhead in distributed settings. Traditional sampling-based approaches mitigate computation load to some extent but often fail to address communication inefficiencies inherent in distributed environments.

openalex-w7221162543.creator: Giovanna Azevedo Rodrigues, Marcelo Eduardo Caixeta
openalex-w7221162543.description: This theoretical article examines the relation between logos, concept, word, proposition and truth from Plato to analytic philosophy and proposes, from the standpoint of Cognitive Psychiatry, a processual reading of epistemology. The method is a qualitative conceptual essay...

pmc-10625251.title: Political instability and hiv/aids response in the south west and north west regions of Cameroon: a qualitative study
pmc-10625251.creator: Julius Enongene Mekolle, Katayi Edouard Tshimwanga, Niba Juste Ongeh, Agbor Nyenty Agbornkwai, Omeichu Agwenam Amadeus, Ismaela Esa, Keshia Ebude Mekolle, Ndung Ako Forbinake, Claude Ngwayu Nkfusai, Pascal Nji Atanga
pmc-10625251.description: BackgroundPolitically motivated violence and insecurity continue to be a major threat to progress in HIV epidemic control and a significant contributor to health inequality. Despite a decreasing HIV/AIDS disease burden, the Republic of Cameroon in West Africa is experiencing ongoing political instability in her North and South West Regions.

pmc-11690809.title: MEASURING INTERGENERATIONAL AMBIVALENCE TOWARD OLDER ADULTS IN THE FAMILY CONTEXT: A SCOPING REVIEW
pmc-11690809.creator: Athena Chung Yin Chan, Sophia Lee, Shuwen Li, Jacquelyn Duckett, Rodlescia Sneed
pmc-11690809.description: Informal family caregivers may frequently feel ambivalent toward taking care of older family members. Ambivalence is the simultaneously held conflicting emotions, cognitions and/or behavioral tendencies due to countervailing expectations about how individual should act within the cultural norms. Most existing measurements directly or indirectly measuring caregiving or intergenerational ambivalence were developed from the West.

pmc-12663318.title: Effects of bromelain supplementation on disease activity and quality of life in patients with ulcerative colitis: a randomized, triple-blind, placebo-controlled study
pmc-12663318.creator: Pedram Delgarm, Marjan Mokhtare, Nasser Ebrahimi Daryani, Jamile Abolghasemi, Seyedeh Tayebeh Rahideh
pmc-12663318.description: Bromelain is a proteolytic enzyme found in pineapple fruit. This study was conducted to evaluate the effects of bromelain supplementation on disease activity and quality of life (QoL) in patients with ulcerative colitis (UC). Seventy individuals with mild-to-moderate UC participated in a randomized, triple-blind clinical trial.

pmc-13045555.title: Syncope in an Athlete With Apical Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
pmc-13045555.creator: Suhas Tatapudi, John-Henry L Dean, Krishna Pabba, Matthew W Martinez
pmc-13045555.description: BackgroundSyncope in athletes with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) requires careful evaluation, as etiologies range from benign to life-threatening. Guidelines emphasize individualized risk stratification and shared decision-making.Case SummaryA 20-year-old basketball player experienced a syncopal episode when rising from a seated position, preceded by progressive lightheadedness and visual dimming, without chest discomfort or palpitations.

pmc-13067627.title: Healthcare trajectories following cancer surgery in older adults: insights from the French health data system
pmc-13067627.creator: Nicolas Bertrand, Héloïse Fauchon, Charline Jean, Estelle Neveu, Thomas Gilbert, Emmanuelle Leray, François Puisieux, Dominique Somme
pmc-13067627.description: Background Healthcare trajectories of older patients with cancer, particularly after surgical treatment, remain poorly described. Understanding these trajectories is crucial for improving patient outcomes and optimizing healthcare resources. This study aimed to describe the one-year healthcare trajectories of older patients following cancer surgery in France and identify their determinants.

pmc-13681764.title: Beyond Recurrence: Impact of Surgical Technique on Testicular Microcirculation After Inguinal Hernia Repair
pmc-13681764.creator: Mehmet Emin Gönüllü, Fatih Gürsoy, İbrahim Feyyaz Naldemir, Erman Yekenkurul, Mehmet Fuat Çetin, Sami Dogan
pmc-13681764.description: BackgroundThe impact of different inguinal hernia repair techniques on testicular perfusion remains a subject of clinical interest. While open and laparoscopic approaches demonstrate comparable outcomes in terms of recurrence and complications, their effects on testicular microcirculation are not fully elucidated.
